geo_headlines: NO STRIKE; TRUMP SAYS DECISION TIME. Trump said Sunday "there won't be a strike today" but that it is "getting to be decision time": "Do I finish it off... or do I make a deal?" (Bloomberg). He has suggested strikes could resume after the November 3 midterms and sent a third carrier group toward the Gulf. Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish defense chiefs meet Iran's leaders in Tehran today (Al Jazeera).

OIL EASES ON MEDIATION. **Brent $114.94 (-1.5%) and December WTI $100.84 (-2.4%), easing from Friday's highest weekly close since 2022 after reports Qatari mediators visited Tehran (Investing.com, Reuters).** Gold $4,025.70 (+0.4%). Goldman calls oil above its forecasts the most important risk for the Fed (Reuters).

FUTURES EDGE UP INTO A BIG WEEK. S&P 500 futures 7,670.25 (+0.14%) and Nasdaq 100 futures 29,125.50 (+0.03%), fading earlier gains of about 0.3%. Tesla +2.1% premarket; CoreWeave and Nebius -3%, both down more than 30% in October (Reuters). The chip index sits at a three-month low after two weeks of losses (Bloomberg).

BRAZIL SHOCK. Lula won a fourth term Sunday in an upset that defied polls; the iShares Brazil ETF is down 27.3% premarket (Reuters). Asia was quiet: Nikkei -0.2%, South Korea -0.5% (down almost 20% this month), Chinese blue chips -0.5% for an 11th straight weekly decline (Reuters).

CENTRAL BANK WEEK. The Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan all decide this week. Markets price a Fed hold Wednesday and about 80% odds of a December hike (Reuters); FedWatch as of Friday 10/23: October 7.8%, December 77.2%. 10-year 5.00%, 2-year 4.69%, 30-year 5.33% (Treasury). Europe opened higher: Stoxx 600 +0.5%, CAC +0.9% (Bloomberg).

TODAY AND THIS WEEK. Verizon before the open; Cadence, Nucor, Welltower and Amkor after (Yahoo Finance). Chicago Fed national activity index (Sept, est. -0.1) and Dallas Fed manufacturing (Oct). Tuesday: Coca-Cola, Boeing, Visa. Wednesday: FOMC 2:00 PM; Alphabet, Microsoft. Thursday: GDP, PCE, Amazon.
client_frame_short: The weekend passed without a strike, and markets are calmer this morning: oil is down about 2% on reports of mediation, and stock futures are slightly higher. **Trump says it is "decision time" between a deal and finishing the war, and he has pointed to after the November 3 midterms, so the oil risk is postponed, not gone.** This week the Fed, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon will matter more for portfolios than any single headline. For clients: stay diversified and rebalanced; plans do not need to change.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is a calmer start to a very busy week, with the Iran decision hanging over oil.

What changed over the weekend: no US strike. Trump said there would be no strike Sunday, called it decision time between a deal and finishing it off, and has pointed to after the November 3 midterms for any renewed attacks. Qatari mediators visited Tehran, and Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish defense chiefs meet Iran's leaders today. Brent eased about 2% to $115.

Where we stand: the S&P 500 is about 2.5% below its October 6 record close after two down weeks. The Nasdaq 100 has been hit harder by AI spending worries, while the Dow has held up. Bonds rallied last week, with the 10-year back to 5.00%.

This week: the Fed decides Wednesday and is expected to hold; markets still lean toward a hike in December. Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday and Amazon Thursday, alongside GDP and PCE inflation. Those reports are the real tests of the AI spending story. About a quarter of S&P 500 companies have reported so far, and analysts describe results as healthy, with resilient demand.

Elsewhere: Brazilian stocks are down sharply after an upset election result, a reminder that emerging-market positions can move a lot on politics and why position sizing matters.

Why it matters: the biggest risks are scheduled (earnings, the Fed) or postponed (Iran), which gives investors time to rebalance calmly rather than react.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and keep bonds working at today's yields. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Friday 5.00%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Friday 5.33%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (now $114.94). Brent is there; strikes are the missing piece, and the timing now points after November 3.
